title: Rava bar Ahilai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He lived approximately in Rav Papa’s time, as in Pesachim 30a: an oven that was plastered with fat — Rava bar Ahilai forbade eating bread [baked in it], even with salt. Ravina said to Rav Ashi: “Since Rava bar Ahilai has been refuted,” etc.

Likewise in Zevachim 10a he challenges Rabbi Yirmeyah’s words and offers another answer, and Rav Ashi challenges it. There, at 16b, he challenges Rava’s words (Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbah bar Ahilai, and so it is in Yuchasin). Hyman infers from this that he lived before Rav Ashi and after Rava.
He is likewise mentioned in Bava Kamma 64b, saying: “What is Rav’s reason, who said that one who admits a fine,” etc.

notes.text: Hyman infers the before-Ashi/after-Rava placement; the Rava/Rabbah variant remains. Rav in the fine-admission question is kept distinct from Rava.

The consulted Pesachim 30a directly names Rava bar Ahilai in the oven-fat ruling. Hyman’s approximate Rav-Papa-era placement, before-Ashi/after-Rava inference and the reported Rabbah reading remain attributed; reporting an earlier authority does not alone establish direct interaction.
